problem: If the sum of the first $36$ terms of an arithmetic series is ${S}_{36}=\frac{225}{2},$ and the last term is ${a}_{36}=\frac{11}{2},$ what is the first term of the series?

feedback.problem: If the sum of the first $20$ terms of an arithmetic series is ${S}_{20}=-635,$ and the last term is ${a}_{20}=-65,$ then the first term of the series is ${a}_{1}=${{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
We are given the last term of our series. So, to find the first term, we use the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series in the form

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{N}{2}({a}_{1}+{a}_{N}),
$$

where ${a}_{1}$ is the first term, ${a}_{N}$ is the last term, and $N$ is the number of terms.

Substituting ${a}_{20}=-65$, $N=20$, and ${S}_{N}=-635$ into the formula above and solving for ${a}_{1}$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-635 & =\frac{20}{2}({a}_{1}+(-65)) \\ -635 & =10({a}_{1}-65) \\ -\frac{635}{10} & ={a}_{1}-65 \\ -63.5 & ={a}_{1}-65 \\ {a}_{1} & =1.5.\end{aligned}
$$
